av_event.line_text: Abdirahman: Erm, I think she just wants a beach. Somewhere warm with a pool.
av_event.what: A young woman in a headscarf walks across the room behind him from left to right carrying two mugs, passing in front of the grey sofa and out of frame. He glances briefly over his shoulder towards her, then looks back at the screen.

text:
B: Hi, can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah, I can hear you. Abdirahman, Leicester.
B: Gareth, Chelmsford. Leicester, I did my degree there, actually. Geography, a long time ago.
A: Oh yeah? Whereabouts did you live?
B: Clarendon Park, second and third year. Queens Road, all those little cafés. Is it still like that?
A: Pretty much, yeah. More coffee places now.
B: Course it is. What do you do?
A: Vehicle technician. Vans at a fleet depot. I'm senior tech on my shift.
B: Nice. Are you getting much electric stuff through now?
A: More and more, yeah. I've done the safety courses, want to get the higher-level ones next. That's where it's all going, you know.
B: Smart. Get ahead of it. I follow Formula One, so I'm sort of fascinated by the battery side. Do you watch it?
A: Not really, to be honest. Football's more my thing. Leicester.
B: Fair enough, I'm the opposite. I'm a travel consultant, by the way, tailor-made trips, mostly Japan and South-East Asia. So my day is basically people telling me where they'd like to go and me working out how to get them there in a bit of style.
A: Right. My wife wants to go to Turkey, actually.
B: Oh, Turkey's great. Where's she thinking? Because Istanbul for a few days, then down to the coast, Kaş or somewhere round there, that's a really nice trip. Or Cappadocia, the balloons at sunrise. I've done that one, it's genuinely worth it.
A: Erm, I think she just wants a beach. Somewhere warm with a pool.
B: Totally doable. Do you know when you'd go?
A: Not really. Depends on work. I'm not that fussed, if I'm honest, I'd rather have a week off at home.
B: Ha, you're not the first person to say that to me today.
A: Yeah, I spoke to the other Gareth. He's the same, his wife books it.
B: Sounds like the wives are doing all the planning in this study. Look, if you do go, avoid the last two weeks of August, the prices go mad. Late September's perfect. Still hot, half the price.
A: Okay. I'll tell her that.
B: What do you do outside work, then? Five-a-side?
A: Yeah, Wednesdays. And I work on my own car. Old Civic. Needs a clutch, so that's my weekend.
B: You're doing a clutch yourself? On a driveway?
A: Yeah, on the road outside. Saves a few hundred quid.
B: I'd have no idea where to start, to be honest. I'm a runner, that's my thing. Training for a marathon, trying to get under three and a half.
A: Fair play. Not for me, that. Five-a-side's enough running.
B: Ha. Do you get much...
